body_markdown:
*Automated workflows reduce vulnerability exposure for over 340 third-party applications from days to minutes*


**BURLINGTON, Massachusetts – October 27, 2026 –**[N-able](https://www.n-able.com/)


, Inc. (NYSE: NABL), a global cybersecurity company delivering business resilience, today announced the launch of AI- a


ccelerated Vulnerability and Patch Management, giving IT teams and service providers a vital defense against increasingly industrialized cybercrime.


AI-accelerated Vulnerability and Patch Management will see enhancements across N-able’s Unified Endpoint Management (UEM) platform that will reduce the patching window from days to minutes. A continuous, closed-loop workflow scans third-party applications for vulnerabilities, prioritizes the most urgent patches, remediates directly without switching tools, and verifies that the update is complete.


Cybercriminals are using AI to change how they operate, creating a new reality for security teams. Vulnerability research that took skilled attackers weeks to complete can now be automated in hours. Exploits are being generated, weaponized, and packaged into attack chains at machine speed. To strengthen defenses, IT teams and service providers need to rethink their approach. A key part of this will be reducing patching windows without complicating logistics or increasing the risk of downtime.


N-able’s patch management workflow will allow IT teams to close that gap through automation and AI-guidance at each step of the process, with no context switching required:


- **Scan: On-demand vulnerability scanning** covers over 900 third-party applications, with automatic remediation of 350+ applications and their thousands of versions—on Windows, macOS, and Linux endpoints. Most vulnerabilities being exploited are in third-party applications, rather than the operating system, making this wide coverage invaluable.


- **Remediate: Patching** is part of the same workflow, eliminating the need to switch to another tool or manual hand-off to a separate patch console, no matter the application or operating system.


New capabilities are available from a single “pane of glass”, along with insights into risk, remediation progress, and patch compliance reports.


“Patching has always been part of IT best practice, but the landscape has changed significantly. AI-assisted exploits mean that human speed simply isn’t enough to stay a step ahead,” said Brendan Griffin, Director of Threat Research at N-able. “AI- a


ccelerated Vulnerability and Patch Management gives IT teams and service providers a key part of the solution, automating the entire patching process from scanning to verification from a single workflow, allowing teams to remediate before the exploit lands.”
